messages:
sam: Quick parity question — ran the private VPC perf suite against on‑prem rack-3 today and tail latency is ~15-25% worse than hosted for long sequences. Anyone seen similar?

mira: Can you paste the exact bench command + a 99/99.9 pctl snippet?

sam: Yep. Command run: `./bench --model=gpt-small --seq=2048 --batch=1 --threads=4 --warmup=200 --runs=100 --kv-cache`
Sample pctl output: `p50 8.3ms, p90 12.1ms, p95 18.4ms, p99 42.7ms, p99.9 78.3ms` — hosted numbers are ~p99 34ms, p99.9 52ms for same commit.

alex: Two quick checks: NIC offload/TSO and MTU mismatch can blow up tail. Also confirm `intel_pstate` governor vs `ondemand`.

tayler: On the rack-3 nodes we had IRQ load balancing on by default (smp_affinity dynamic). If the KV cache threads are pinned, IRQs can preempt them.

perf-bot: Suggestion: enable hugepages + disable HT for a run. Historical wins on long-seq workloads.

mira: I can run a flamegraph/profile tomorrow. Do you have the perf script and root access?

sam: I have perf data collected (compressed) — will upload to the shared bucket. No root on the test fleet; need ops help to spin a cluster with `nohz_full` and `isolcpus` set like hosted.

ops-bot: @ops can provision a parity node with kernel params: `nohz_full=1 isolcpus=4-7 rcu_nocbs=4-7 intel_pstate=disable` and match MTU 9000. ETA ~2h.

mira: Perfect. Once we have a parity node I'll: 1) re-run bench w/ `perf record --call-graph=dwarf`, 2) capture irqbalance status, 3) dump `ethtool -k` and `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_*`.

alex: Also check CPU freq scaling during runs: `watch -n0.5 \"cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_cur_freq\"` — if it oscillates you'll see tail spikes.

sam: Noted. One weird data point: the discrepancy appears only when KV cache is warm — cold start p99s line up closely. Makes me think of scheduling / cache eviction on NUMA.

tayler: If it helps, I'll drop in a small NUMA binding shim to force allocation on the GPU's local node and re-run. Low-risk.

mira: I'll queue the flamegraph + a quick `numactl --show` check after ops spins the node. Sam, upload the perf tarball and bench stdout to the bucket and add the link here.

sam: Uploaded: gs://redwood-test/perf/rack3-run-1930054321.tar.gz — contains bench stdout, `/proc/cpuinfo`, `dmesg` tail, and perf.data.

ops-bot: Provisioned node: rack3-parity-01. Kernel bootline: `... nohz_full=1 isolcpus=4-7 rcu_nocbs=4-7 intel_pstate=disable` MTU 9000 set. SSH jump available to `eng-runtime`.

mira: Starting profile run now. Will post flamegraph link when done (~45m).

alex: If flamegraph shows heavy IRQ or syscall time in the worker threads that points at NIC or scheduler issues.

sam: Thanks all — will watch the thread and help validate. If we confirm a systemic diff we can add a quick parity test to CI to catch regressions. :thumbsup:

mira: Flamegraph posted: https://perf.redwood/fg/1930054321 — initial look shows a few syscalls in the critical path and some `__cpufreq_driver` activity correlated with p99 spikes.

tayler: Good find. I'll prepare the numa-bind shim and test with cpufreq governor forced to `performance`.

sam: OK plan: ops will snapshot config, tayler runs numa-bind + performance governor, mira re-runs profile, alex verifies NIC offload settings. We iterate from there.

mira: I'll also add a quick micro-benchmark to exercise kv-cache locality (small loops that warm the cache) to reproduce locally.

sam: Great. Thanks everyone — will follow up with a short postmortem if we pin root cause.
